subject: Banking
title: Personal Loans vs. Credit Cards
description: Learn Personal Loans vs. Credit Cards in one minute.

hook.text: Personal loans charge 8-12% interest. Credit cards charge 24%. For carrying debt, personal loans save thousands.

buildup.text: Personal loans have fixed payments over 2-5 years. Credit cards have variable rates and no fixed end date.

discovery.text: Debt consolidation loans let you roll multiple card balances into one lower-rate payment.

twist.text: 40% of people who consolidate credit card debt run up new card balances.

climax.text: Lower rates help only if behavior changes. Consolidation without discipline just adds a new loan on top of old ones.

punchline.text: 12% beats 24%. But 40% of consolidators run up new card debt anyway.

quiz.question: What happens to 40% of people after debt consolidation?
options: They accumulate new credit card balances

details.summary: Personal loans provide a fixed amount at a fixed interest rate repaid over a set period, while credit cards offer revolving credit at variable rates. Choosing between them depends on the purpose, amount, and your repayment discipline.
details.whyItMatters: Using the wrong type of credit costs thousands in unnecessary interest. Personal loans are generally cheaper for large purchases you can repay on schedule, while credit cards offer flexibility but punish those who carry balances.
takeaways: Personal loans offer fixed rates typically 6 to 36 percent versus card rates above 20 percent
Fixed payment schedules force disciplined repayment with personal loans
Credit cards offer flexibility and rewards but tempt overspending

faq.question: When should you use a personal loan instead of a credit card?
faq.answer: For large purchases over a few thousand dollars, debt consolidation, or any situation where you know the exact amount needed and want predictable payments. The fixed rate and forced payoff schedule save money versus carrying a credit card balance.

faq.question: Does taking a personal loan hurt your credit score?
faq.answer: Initially, yes. The hard inquiry and new account lower your score slightly. But over time, on-time payments build positive history, and the added credit mix may improve your score. Using it to pay off cards improves utilization too.
